quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Work as well as a face shield.
Provide the same protection as a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield protects your entire face and is better than goggles. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. These signs tell riders about road rules they must follow.

questions.question: Experienced riders use IPDE to make safe decisions while riding. What does the "P" stand for?
questions.explanation: IPDE stands for Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute. Experienced riders use this system to stay safe.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, motorcycle riders should look over their shoulders because:

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
It helps other drivers notice you.
You should make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always look over your shoulder to check for vehicles or hazards before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert riders to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because riders and other drivers can collide there. Many accidents happen at intersections.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield provides the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. A windshield alone is not enough either, though it may reduce requirements.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control the motorcycle and should be avoided.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Experienced riders use IPDE to make safe decisions while riding. What does the "D" stand for?
questions.explanation: IPDE stands for Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute. Experienced riders use this system to stay safe.

questions.question: Which material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for riders. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: What can you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight to be more visible at intersections. Ride in a lane position that helps you see oncoming traffic. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: For maximum protection, your helmet should be certified by the:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for maximum protection.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder
In the part of the lane where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror
As close to the car as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Ride in a position where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually this means riding in the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors, so this position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do
You should only use them when other vehicles are nearby
They are more complicated than signals on a car

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are at higher risk. Use your turn signals to tell others what you plan to do. Always use them when you change lanes or turn, even if no one else is nearby.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle rider should be prepared for:

options.text: A parked car to suddenly pull out into traffic
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car to suddenly pull out into traffic
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space between your motorcycle and any dangers.

questions.question: What can reduce your risk of a crash?

options.text: Tell other road users what you plan to do
Ride in parts of the lane where you are hard to see

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other road users what you plan to do
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your plans. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road in front, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can:

options.text: Be acceptable as long as you stay under the speed limit
Be safer on a motorcycle than in a car
Be acceptable if no other vehicles are nearby
Cause you to move into another lane or leave the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause you to move into another lane or leave the road
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may end up in another lane or even leave the road. Use caution when turning.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Rhode Island, anyone with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Which fabric provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding and try to stay awake.

questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: Which statement about low-speed crashes is true?

options.text: They happen often, so you don't need to worry.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can cause death.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?

options.text: Oil strip in the center of a lane

questions.explanation: Many surfaces cause poor tire grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, oil, and metal plates are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: Why should you wear a leather jacket when riding?

options.text: It is too warm in hot weather.
It protects you in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket while riding for protection. Leather jackets help protect you even in warm weather and are made to keep you cool.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It contains details about how to operate it and how to maintain it.
